summary: Frontend-only test of [KODA_VAD_TRACE] emission on web preview. ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED via code inspection: the [KODA_VAD_TRACE] console.log block exists ONLY in the native code path of /app/frontend/lib/voice.ts (lines 519-538, inside the setInterval starting at line 504, which is reached only after the `if (Platform.OS === 'web')` branch at lines 276-412 returns). The WEB branch has its own separate VAD setInterval (lines 319-353) and emits NO trace logging. Therefore the web preview at localhost:3000 / preview URL will NEVER produce [KODA_VAD_TRACE] lines, regardless of whether the rename + filter widening fix is applied. The user reports the issue on TestFlight (native iOS) — so the rename to [KODA_VAD_TRACE] and the diagLogger.ts CAPTURE_PREFIXES widening LOOK correct for native, but I could not validate native behaviour from the web sandbox. SECONDARY BUG FOUND: identifier `adaptiveMode` is assigned at voice.ts:577, 581, 588 but NEVER declared (no let/var/const). TypeScript reports TS2304. In strict-mode ESM (which Metro emits) this is a runtime ReferenceError thrown inside the calibration branch of the native VAD interval. The throw is silently swallowed by the catch at line 639, so the bug is INVISIBLE in logs — but it aborts calibration before `silenceThresholdEff` / `sustainedThresholdEff` get updated to adaptive values, AND on every subsequent frame the same throw happens BEFORE the KODA_VAD_TRACE console.log line. Wait — actually the trace log is at lines 519-538, BEFORE the calibration block (line 546+), so trace WILL print pre-calibration. But once `calibrationDone` becomes true in some prior frame, the next frame goes through the post-calibration block (line 596+) which does NOT touch adaptiveMode, so trace continues. However IN the calibration-completion frame itself, adaptiveMode = ... throws and the `console.log` for [KODA_VAD_CALIB] never runs for that branch. Bottom line: trace logs should still appear on native, but CALIB log is broken. CORS BLOCKER also found: backend returns `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (preflight) but the frontend uses `credentials: 'include'` → browser blocks ALL authenticated calls including /api/auth/dev-login → web preview login fails with 'Dev login non riuscito.' I could NOT log into the app to actually start a recording.

critical.issue: CORS misconfigured: returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with no Allow-Credentials, but frontend sends credentials:'include'. Browser blocks every preflight → dev login (and likely every authenticated call) impossible from a real browser. curl works because curl ignores CORS.

integration_issues.issue: CORS preflight blocked → 'Dev login non riuscito.' Cannot proceed to voice testing on web.

react_native_issues.issue: [KODA_VAD_TRACE] console.log is emitted ONLY in the native (Platform.OS !== 'web') branch (voice.ts lines 519-538). The web branch (lines 276-412) has its own setInterval VAD loop (lines 319-353) and emits NO trace logging. Testing on web preview will NEVER show [KODA_VAD_TRACE]. Reference: /app/frontend/lib/voice.ts:319-353 vs 519-538.

Identifier `adaptiveMode` is assigned (= false / = true) at lines 577, 581, 588 but is NEVER declared. TS2304. In strict-mode ESM this throws ReferenceError which is silently swallowed by the outer try/catch at line 639. Side effect: in the adaptive branch, `silenceThresholdEff` / `speechThresholdEff` / `sustainedThresholdEff` updates that follow the `adaptiveMode = true` assignment (line 581 → 582) are NEVER reached, so the adaptive VAD thresholds remain at static defaults. The [KODA_VAD_CALIB] log line for that frame also never fires. This is plausibly part of the original 'VAD non chiude in furgone' bug. Reference: /app/frontend/lib/voice.ts:577, 581, 588.

Footer text on /diagnostics says 'Cattura: [KODA_VAD] [KODA_TIMING] [KODA_SUMMARY]' which does not mention [KODA_VAD_TRACE] or the legacy [VAD_*] / [AUDIO_HONESTY*] prefixes that diagLogger.ts now captures. Cosmetic but misleading for the tester. Reference: /app/frontend/app/diagnostics.tsx:104.

action_items: PRIMARY FIX (main agent): add the same `if (VAD_TRACE_ENABLED) console.log('[KODA_VAD_TRACE] ...')` block inside the WEB setInterval at /app/frontend/lib/voice.ts lines 319-353 so testers on the Expo web preview can validate the diagnostic on localhost:3000. Without this, the web sandbox can never reproduce the user's TestFlight scenario.

SECONDARY FIX (main agent): declare `let adaptiveMode = false;` near the other VAD state vars (~line 484) in /app/frontend/lib/voice.ts. This unblocks the adaptive-threshold path that the calibration was supposed to enable for noisy environments (furgone). This is very possibly contributing to the 'VAD non chiude in furgone' symptom the trace was added to diagnose in the first place.

BACKEND FIX (main agent): fix CORS — either return the request Origin echoed back and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, or change frontend jsonReq to `credentials: 'omit'` (it already passes session_token in body/header). Without this, web preview cannot dev-login → no testing agent can ever exercise the voice flow on web.
COSMETIC: update /app/frontend/app/diagnostics.tsx:104 'statsTextDim' label to include [KODA_VAD_TRACE] and [VAD_*] / [AUDIO_HONESTY*] so the user knows what is captured.

VALIDATION ON DEVICE: confirm on a real TestFlight build that AFTER the rename, [KODA_VAD_TRACE] lines now appear in /diagnostics. The fix in diagLogger.ts (adding '[VAD_' and '[AUDIO_HONESTY' prefixes to CAPTURE_PREFIXES) is correct and backward-compatible — it will pick up any leftover [VAD_TRACE] emissions from older builds too.
critical_code_review_comments: voice.ts is 743 lines and contains 4+ years of inline change-log comments — consider extracting the native VAD interval into its own module (e.g. lib/vad.ts) to make further diagnostic edits less error-prone.

The web and native VAD loops have diverged significantly (different state machines, different thresholds, only native has calibration + trace). A shared `evaluateVadFrame(db, state)` pure function would prevent this kind of 'fix applied to one path, not the other' bug.
Silent `catch (e) {}` at voice.ts:639 hides real bugs (the adaptiveMode ReferenceError is invisible). At minimum log `e` with a [KODA_VAD_ERR] prefix so it lands in the diag buffer.

success_rate.frontend: 0% — could not log in due to CORS; KODA_VAD_TRACE confirmed missing from web code path by inspection

context_for_next_testing_agent: Web preview dev-login is blocked by CORS (wildcard origin + credentials:include incompatibility). To test KODA_VAD_TRACE you EITHER need (a) the main agent to fix CORS + add the trace log to the web VAD branch, OR (b) test on a native build (Expo Go QR + iPhone). The native trace block at voice.ts:519-538 is correctly written and uses the [KODA_VAD_TRACE] prefix that diagLogger captures via the '[KODA_' entry in CAPTURE_PREFIXES — so once a recording actually runs on native, lines SHOULD appear in /diagnostics. The previously emitted [VAD_TRACE] / [VAD_CALIB] / [AUDIO_HONESTY*] strings are also now captured by diagLogger's widened filter (correct).
rca_of_issue: User reports [KODA_VAD_TRACE] missing from exported diag log after TestFlight build. Two independent root causes found by code inspection: (1) the trace console.log is only inside the native branch of startRecording(), so any sandbox test on Expo web (localhost:3000) will produce zero trace lines even when the recording is running — but this does NOT explain the TestFlight gap. (2) The undeclared `adaptiveMode` (voice.ts:577/581/588) throws a swallowed ReferenceError exactly at calibration-completion frame; while the trace log line itself is upstream of this throw and should still fire, this bug means adaptive-mode thresholds never get applied, so the original 'VAD non chiude in furgone' symptom may persist even with the trace working. RECOMMENDED MITIGATION: (a) declare `let adaptiveMode = false;` so adaptive thresholds activate; (b) duplicate the trace log into the web VAD branch so future regression tests can run on the sandbox; (c) on a fresh TestFlight build, open /diagnostics AFTER recording a 10-15s utterance — if still empty, the issue is somewhere between console.log and diagLogger.installDiagLogger (verify _layout.tsx still installs it on cold start and that no other module reassigns console.log after); (d) fix CORS so web-based test agents can fully validate the flow.
